chain.label: No FAA surveillance of Part 91 parachute operator; TBO compliance not required
chain.trigger: a review of FAA Program Tracking and Reporting Subsystem data and Safety Performance Analysis System data showed no record of FAA inspectors conducting any maintenance or operations surveillance visits to the operator

chain.label: Engines operated thousands of hours past recommended TBO; discrepancies left unrepaired
chain.trigger: the left and right engines had accumulated 5,829 hours and 6,493 hours since overhaul, respectively ... which far exceeded the manufacturer's recommended time between overhaul (TBO) period of 3,600 hours

caused_by.evidence: greater FAA surveillance of the operator would have discouraged improper aircraft maintenance procedures

chain.label: Undetected initiating condition in right engine compressor turbine section
chain.trigger: it is possible that the initiating fracture event within the engine resulted from a condition that could have been detected and corrected during an engine overhaul performed within the manufacturer's recommended TBO

caused_by.evidence: Overhauling an engine within the manufacturers' recommended TBO increases the likelihood that potentially catastrophic conditions that may otherwise be undetectable will be discovered and corrected

chain.label: Pilot chose intersection takeoff using only 1,700 ft of the 4,500-ft runway
chain.trigger: the pilot taxied the airplane onto runway 24 from the intersecting taxiway, which is about 1,700 feet from the runway's west end, and began a takeoff roll to the west from that location, rather than using the runway's entire 4,500-foot length

chain.label: Power loss occurred just after liftoff at treetop height with minimal altitude and time
chain.trigger: a loss of engine power during takeoff is a critical emergency because altitude and time are minimal

chain.label: Right engine compressor turbine blade overload fracture and loss of power
chain.trigger: the right engine's compressor turbine disk was intact but that its attached blades were fractured; the damage observed within the engine resulted in the loss of engine power

caused_by.evidence: the initial blade separation originated within the compressor turbine section

chain.label: Pilot failed to execute engine-failure memory items (no rudder, no bank toward live engine)
chain.trigger: evidence showed that the accident pilot failed to effectively perform most of those procedures. For example ... the airplane's rudder was not deflected and its wings were not banked toward the operating engine

caused_by.evidence: the emergency procedures for an engine failure during takeoff include, in part: ... Maintain heading by applying rudder and lowering wing against the live engine

chain.label: Pilot allowed drift toward the inoperative engine and let airspeed decay
chain.trigger: the pilot instead allowed the airplane to drift to the right (toward the inoperative engine) before it nose-dived into the ground

caused_by.evidence: the pilot used poor technique by not banking the airplane or using rudder control to maintain airspeed as prescribed in the airplane's emergency procedures

chain.label: Airspeed decayed to aerodynamic stall
chain.trigger: the pilot allowed the airplane's airspeed to decay to the point of aerodynamic stall

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's failure to maintain airspeed ... negated any possibility of continued, controlled flight
engine wear would likely have prevented the accident airplane from obtaining its maximum published single-engine climb performance

chain.label: Uncontrolled nose-down descent
chain.trigger: the nose-down attitude of the wreckage, and the crush damage to the forward fuselage of the airplane are consistent with an uncontrolled descent due to an aerodynamic stall

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's descent was not controlled

chain.label: Single-point sidewall restraints provided no upper-body support for parachutists
chain.trigger: a single-point restraint system is not sufficient to provide adequate restraint for parachutists

chain.label: Airplane dived nose first into trees and terrain about 1/2 mile northwest of runway 24
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted trees and terrain and came to rest vertically, nose down against a tree behind a residence about 1/2 mile northwest of the end of runway 24

caused_by.evidence: she saw the airplane flying straight and level but very low over the trees before it dived nose first to the ground

the pilot's decision to use only 1,700 feet of the available runway diminished the margin of safety during takeoff because it eliminated the option of discontinuing the takeoff and performing a straight-ahead, emergency landing on the runway

chain.label: Pilot and five parachutists killed; two parachutists seriously injured
chain.trigger: The pilot and five parachutists were killed, and two parachutists were seriously injured

caused_by.evidence: only the space where the pilot was seated was subjected to nonsurvivable crush intrusion

Lack of support for the upper body and head, slack in the restraints, and any restraint and/or harness stretch during the accident sequence enabled forward motion of each restrained parachutist into the region of intrusion and/or into other parachutists. These types of issues contributed to the severity of the injuries
